content.comment_body: Hello, I hope you are doing well. I am having trouble and would appreciate your assistance. 1. We have an HVAC system installed with [product_name] [version_no]. When attempting to access the program via [product_name] [version_no], it prompts for a password. Is it necessary to downgrade the [product_name] software to [version_no] to open programs on [product_name] [version_no]? 2. We also have a new [product_name] [version_no] device and are trying to upload a backup created with [product_name] [version_no]. The password prompt appears again. We attempted to export the program from [product_name] [version_no] and upload it to the newer device but still encounter a password prompt. Your help would be greatly appreciated. Thank you in advance.
Was a password originally set for the [version_no] software? Is the unencrypted source available?

If you do not know the password, it is not possible to access the program. It is best to contact the original program creator to request the password. Downgrading the [product_name] software will likely not resolve this issue.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are unable to access or modify programs created in [product_name] [version_no] without the correct password, regardless of attempting to use other versions of [product_name] software or devices. Password protection and program encryption set during the initial creation are preventing transfer and export between older and newer hardware and software versions, causing frustration and workflow interruptions.
analysis.user_expectations: Users anticipate straightforward access, transfer, and management of program files between different [product_name] software and hardware versions, without unexpected password prompts or restrictions.
